intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, white sand, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boats depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets in Monastiraki. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek street food like souvlaki and spanakopita. Engage with local vendors and discover authentic Greek culinary culture.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade through the warm, calm waters of the lagoon and relax on one of Greece's most beautiful and unique beaches. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Chania's Old Town to learn how to prepare authentic Cretan dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and loukoumades (honey fritters). Classes typically include a market visit to source fresh local ingredients and a full meal at the end.

experiences.name: Sunset Dinner at a Traditional Taverna in Oia
experiences.description: Experience the world-famous Santorini sunset from the village of Oia while dining at a cliffside taverna. Enjoy fresh grilled octopus, fava (yellow split pea dip), fresh fish, and local Assyrtiko wine as the sun dips below the caldera. Book a table in advance for the best views and a truly memorable evening.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X96 express bus or metro to connect to your transfer toward Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In flight
meals.lunch: N/A - In flight
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night gyro or souvlaki wrap from a 24-hour street kiosk near the airport or transfer point (€3–5). Perfect budget bite after a long journey.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your carry-on snacks handy for the journey. The X96 bus from Athens airport to Piraeus costs around €6 and runs 24 hours. Exchange a small amount of euros before leaving the airport. Rest is the priority tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a slow start, take a leisurely walk along the beachfront promenade directly in front of Aegean Bliss Resort. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea for the first time and scout the local area. Visit a nearby bakery for a traditional Greek breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on the resort's beach or the nearest public beach. Swim in the warm sea (water temp around 24–25°C), sunbathe, and relax. Explore the immediate shoreline and get your bearings around the local neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest village or town center for a casual evening walk. Browse local shops and find a traditional taverna for dinner. Watch the sunset over the water from the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Visit a local bakery (φούρνος) for a cheese or spinach pie (tiropita/spanakopita) and a Greek coffee — budget around €3–4.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic from a local mini-market: olives, feta, bread, tomatoes, and water for around €5–6.
meals.dinner: Find a local taverna away from the tourist strip. Order a Greek salad and grilled fish of the day (psari) or moussaka. Budget €10–13 per person including a local beer.

day_by_day.notes: Today is purely a recovery and orientation day. Don't overplan — let yourself ease into Greek rhythm. Most beaches in Greece are free to access. Bring reef-safe sunscreen as UV index is very high in June.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and head to the nearest local market (laiki agora) if one is running — these open-air markets typically operate in the morning and are perfect for picking up fresh fruit, vegetables, local honey, and cheap snacks. Great way to interact with locals and experience authentic Greek daily life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby hidden or less-touristy beach cove accessible by local bus or a short walk. Spend the afternoon swimming, snorkeling, and exploring rock pools. Bring your picnic supplies from the morning market.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and explore the local harbor (if nearby). Sit at a waterfront café for an ouzo or local wine at sunset. Then find a psarotaverna (fish taverna) for a budget seafood dinner.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit, yogurt with honey, and a coffee from the laiki market stalls — approximately €4–5.
meals.lunch: Market picnic on the beach: fresh bread, local cheese, tomatoes, olives, and fruit — approximately €5–7.
meals.dinner: Psarotaverna dinner: grilled octopus or calamari with a side of tzatziki and pita bread. Budget €11–14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Local markets usually run Tuesday, Friday, or Saturday mornings depending on the area — check locally. Bring a reusable bag to the market. Ouzo is traditionally served with a small plate of mezedes (snacks) at no extra charge in many traditional spots.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or shared taxi to explore a nearby historic village or archaeological site within the region. Walk through cobblestone streets, visit a small Byzantine church, and admire traditional whitewashed architecture. Many small local museums have free or very low-cost entry (€2–4).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the village. Find a shaded square (plateia) and rest like a local during the hottest part of the day (2–4 PM). Browse small artisan shops for affordable local crafts, herbs, and spices as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by late afternoon. Enjoy a refreshing swim before dinner. Head out for dinner at a family-run taverna — these typically offer the best value and most authentic food.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or a nearby café: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts plus a freddo cappuccino — €4–6.
meals.lunch: Eat at a village kafeneion (traditional Greek café): simple dishes like bean soup (fasolada), bread, and a soft drink — €6–8.
meals.dinner: Family taverna: lamb kleftiko or stuffed tomatoes (gemista) with a carafe of house wine. Budget €10–13 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for cobblestone village streets. Carry a water bottle — staying hydrated in 29°C heat is essential. Most churches require covered shoulders and knees — carry a light scarf.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning — head out early (before 9 AM) to claim a great spot before it gets crowded. The sea is warmest and calmest in the morning. Try snorkeling along rocky outcrops to spot sea urchins, small fish, and starfish. Bring your own snorkel gear or rent cheaply locally.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus ride to a different beach in the area — variety is key! Look for a beach with a beach bar where you can get a cold drink and shade. Try paddleboarding or kayaking if rentals are available at an affordable rate (€8–12/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at a clifftop or beachfront bar. Then dinner at a mezedopoleio (meze restaurant) where you can share multiple small dishes — perfect for sampling many Greek flavors without overspending.

meals.breakfast: Simple hotel breakfast or grab a koulouria (sesame bread ring) from a street vendor for €0.50–1 plus a takeaway coffee.
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar: a toasted sandwich (tost) with ham and cheese or a gyro wrap — €3–5.
meals.dinner: Mezedopoleio: order 4–5 shared meze plates (dolmades, taramasalata, saganaki, grilled vegetables, meatballs). Budget €10–12 per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Going to the beach early means cooler temperatures, fewer crowds, and better parking/bus seats. Many beach bars have a minimum spend policy — check before sitting. Sharing meze dishes is the authentic Greek way to dine.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip by local ferry or bus to a nearby island or coastal town (depending on your resort's location). Ferries in Greece are very affordable for short hops (€5–15 each way). Explore the new destination's port area and main street in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find the best beach at the day-trip destination and spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing. Explore any free viewpoints, windmills, or scenic spots the location is known for.
day_by_day.evening: Head back on the return ferry or bus before sunset. Enjoy the sea views during the journey. Have a relaxed dinner near the resort upon return.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure: a quick spanakopita and coffee from a bakery — €3–4.
meals.lunch: At the day-trip destination: fresh seafood at a harbor-side restaurant — grilled sardines (sardeles) are extremely affordable and delicious. Budget €8–10.
meals.dinner: Back at base: a simple souvlaki plate with tzatziki, pita, and fries from a local souvlatzidiko — €7–9.

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry timetables the day before and book early morning departure to maximize time at the destination. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water for the ferry journey. Return ferries can fill up in peak season — aim to be at the port 30 minutes early.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip rest and recharge day. Sleep in, have a slow breakfast, and spend the morning journaling, reading, or swimming quietly at the hotel beach. Take a gentle walk along the shoreline and collect sea glass or shells.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local food scene more deeply. Visit a local supermarket (AB Vassilopoulos, Sklavenitis, or Lidl) and put together a Greek feast of ingredients: feta, olives, fresh bread, cured meats, and local wine — perfect for a balcony or beach picnic.
day_by_day.evening: Cook or assemble your supermarket feast on the hotel balcony or at a beach picnic spot for a very budget-friendly dinner. This is a great way to save money mid-trip. Watch the stars come out over the Aegean.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed hotel breakfast or a full Greek yogurt bowl with granola and honey — €4–5 from a café.
meals.lunch: Light lunch: a Greek salad (horiatiki) at a beachside café — €6–8.
meals.dinner: DIY supermarket picnic: feta, olives, cured meats, crusty bread, cherry tomatoes, and a bottle of local wine (Assyrtiko or Agiorgitiko). Total cost: €10–14 for two people.

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally low-key to prevent travel burnout. Greek supermarkets stock excellent local products at a fraction of restaurant prices. Local wine is very affordable — a decent bottle costs €4–8 in supermarkets.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise swim — one of the most magical experiences in Greece. After, take a morning hike or coastal walk along a scenic trail near the resort. Many Greek coastal areas have marked paths with stunning sea views. Bring water and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local fishing village if one is within reach. Watch the fishermen bring in their catch, browse the small harbor, and chat with locals. This is authentic Greece at its best and completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at a harbor-side taverna in the fishing village or back near the resort. Order the fresh catch of the day — whatever the fishermen brought in that morning will be the freshest and often the best-priced option.

meals.breakfast: Pre-swim: a banana and water. Post-swim: a proper breakfast at a café — scrambled eggs, toast, and coffee — €5–7.
meals.lunch: At the fishing village: fried calamari and a cold Mythos beer at a simple harbor café — €8–10.
meals.dinner: Fresh catch of the day (whole grilled fish, priced by the kilo — ask the price first), with a Greek salad and house wine. Budget €12–16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sunrise in Greece in June is around 6:00–6:15 AM — worth the early alarm. Always ask the price per kilo for fresh fish before ordering to avoid surprise bills. Bring insect repellent for evening outdoor dining.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to learning about Greek food culture. Take a self-guided walking food tour of the nearest town: visit the local bakery, the butcher, the olive oil shop, and the spice market. Sample as you go and pick up affordable local products to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the beach for a long, lazy afternoon swim session. Try to find a quieter cove or stretch of beach away from the main tourist areas. Bring a good book and embrace the dolce far niente (the pleasure of doing nothing) — a very Greek concept.
day_by_day.evening: Try a different type of Greek restaurant tonight — a psistaria (grill house) specializing in meat. Order grilled lamb chops (paidakia) or chicken souvlaki skewers with pita and tzatziki.

meals.breakfast: Samples from the food tour bakeries and shops — budget €4–6 for tastings and a coffee.
meals.lunch: Simple taverna lunch: a bowl of revithia (chickpea soup) or lentil soup with crusty bread — €5–7. Very filling and nutritious.
meals.dinner: Psistaria grill house: lamb chops, grilled pita, tzatziki, and a village salad. Budget €11–14 per person with a cold beer.

day_by_day.notes: Buying local olive oil, herbs, and honey from small producers makes excellent and very affordable souvenirs. Greek chickpea and lentil soups are underrated gems — cheap, hearty, and delicious. Psistaria restaurants often have a minimum charge per person — check the menu.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longer excursion today by local bus to a well-known beach or coastal attraction in the wider region. Research the top-rated free or low-cost beaches within 1–2 hours of the resort. Arrive early to secure a good spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the full afternoon at this destination beach. If boat tours to sea caves or snorkeling spots depart from here, consider joining one — group boat trips often cost €15–25 and are well worth the experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort in the early evening. Have a relaxing shower and then enjoy dinner at a restaurant you've been wanting to try since arriving — perhaps the best-reviewed local spot you've been saving.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast to eat on the bus: a tiropita, fruit, and a coffee in a to-go cup — €3–4.
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at the destination: a gyro or a cheese pie with a cold drink — €5–7.
meals.dinner: Best local taverna: a full spread including mezedes, main course, dessert, and local wine. Treat yourself slightly — budget €14–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Research bus schedules the evening before. Local KTEL buses are very affordable (€2–8 depending on distance) and offer a great way to see the countryside. Boat trips to sea caves are a highlight of Greek travel — book directly at the harbor to avoid agency markups.

day_by_day.morning: Morning dedicated to Greek coffee culture. Find a traditional kafeneion and sit for at least an hour with a Greek coffee (ellinikos kafes) or frappe. Watch local life go by. Then take a gentle walk through residential streets to see non-touristy local life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit any free local attractions: a small archaeological site, a hilltop chapel, or a scenic viewpoint accessible on foot or by local bus. Bring your camera — the views of the Aegean from elevated points are spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Penultimate full evening — celebrate with a proper Greek feast. Find a restaurant offering traditional live Greek music (rembetika or laika) if possible, as some tavernas host live music nights for free.

meals.breakfast: At the kafeneion: Greek coffee and a loukoumades (honey doughnut balls) — €3–4.
meals.lunch: Supermarket or bakery lunch: fresh bread, local cheese, and fruit eaten at a scenic viewpoint — €4–6.
meals.dinner: Traditional feast taverna: start with taramasalata and bread, follow with slow-cooked lamb or beef stifado (stew), end with complimentary dessert (many tavernas offer free dessert or shots of raki). Budget €12–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Greek coffee is served very strong and thick — don't drink the grounds at the bottom of the cup. Rembetika is the Greek equivalent of the blues — soulful and authentic. Ask your hotel reception about which local tavernas host music nights.

day_by_day.morning: Last full beach day! Head to your favorite beach discovered during the trip for a final long swim. Reflect on the journey and soak in the beautiful Aegean scenery. Try to get in the water as much as possible.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any last-minute souvenir shopping in the afternoon when the heat is at its peak and you need shade anyway. Focus on affordable authentic Greek products: local honey, thyme or oregano, olive oil soap, ceramic magnets, or worry beads (komboloi).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best taverna you've found during the trip. Order all your favorite dishes from the past 12 days. Toast to Greece with a glass of local wine or ouzo.

meals.breakfast: A full sit-down breakfast at a beachfront café: eggs, toast, fruit, and a freddo espresso — €6–8. Treat yourself on the last full day.
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch: a gyro wrap and a cold drink — €4–6. Keep it simple to save appetite for dinner.
meals.dinner: Farewell feast: your favorite Greek dishes revisited — Greek salad, saganaki, grilled fish or lamb, local wine, and a complimentary raki or dessert. Budget €14–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight to avoid morning stress. Separate any liquids or olive oil purchases into checked luggage. Keep a small amount of euros for airport expenses. Leave a review for your favorite local tavernas online — it helps small family businesses enormously.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — check out time depending on your flight. If you have time before checkout, take one last sunrise walk along the beach or a final dip in the Aegean Sea. Breathe in the sea air and commit the views to memory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and begin your journey to the airport. Allow plenty of time for transfers. If you have a late flight, store luggage at the hotel and explore the local area one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — board your flight home with a suitcase full of local products, a camera full of memories, and a deep appreciation for Greek food, beaches, and hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast: a spanakopita and a strong Greek coffee at a local bakery near the hotel — €3–4.
meals.lunch: Airport or transit lunch: grab a souvlaki or gyro wrap from a local spot before heading to the airport rather than paying airport prices — €4–6.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal. If time permits before security, find a sit-down restaurant in the airport departures area — budget €10–15.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security at Greek airports in peak summer season. Athens airport has a large duty-free area with Greek products at reasonable prices for last-minute gifts. Kalo taxidi — have a good journey!

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange private transfer or take the X96 express bus to your coastal connection. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and unwind with a welcome drink at the hotel bar.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In flight
meals.lunch: N/A - In flight
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the hotel bar or a quick gyros wrap from a 24-hour souvlaki stand near the transfer point (€4–6)

day_by_day.notes: Keep carry-on essentials handy for a smooth late-night arrival. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid delays. Exchange some euros at the airport for small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a slow orientation walk along the beachfront promenade to get your bearings and spot nearby tavernas and shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest local beach. Rent a sunbed and umbrella (€8–12) and take your first dip in the warm Aegean Sea. Explore the shoreline on foot and scout snorkeling spots for later in the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest village for your first authentic Greek dinner. Find a family-run taverna with outdoor seating and order mezedes to share.

meals.breakfast: Hotel buffet breakfast — fresh bread, local honey, yogurt with fruit, eggs, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Casual beachside snack bar — toasted sandwich, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and a Greek salad (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Local taverna — grilled octopus, tzatziki, village salad, and a carafe of house white wine (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Apply high-SPF sunscreen from day one — the Greek June sun is intense. Stay hydrated throughout the day. This is a gentle re-entry day to ease into the trip rhythm.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby archaeological site or hilltop chapel in the cool morning hours. Enjoy panoramic views of the coastline and surrounding landscape. Many smaller sites have free or low-cost entry (€0–6).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beach for swimming and relaxation. Try renting a kayak or paddleboard from a local water sports operator to explore the cove from the water (€15–20/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Join a sunset-watching gathering at a clifftop bar or waterfront café. Order a local Mythos beer or a glass of ouzo with a small plate of olives while watching the sun dip into the sea.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery — spanakopita (spinach pie) and a freddo cappuccino (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Beachside kiosk or snack bar — souvlaki skewers, pita bread, and a cold Fanta lemon (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Waterfront seafood restaurant — grilled sea bream, lemon potatoes, and a shared bottle of Assyrtiko white wine (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book water sports equipment early in the morning to secure afternoon availability. The hilltop sites are best visited before 10:00 AM before the heat peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day boat trip or ferry to a nearby secluded beach or small islet accessible only by water. These hidden coves typically have crystal-clear turquoise water ideal for snorkeling (boat hire €20–40 per person for shared trips).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the secluded beach, snorkeling, swimming, and picnicking. Bring water, sunscreen, and light snacks from a local minimarket.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and freshen up. Explore the hotel's amenities — pool, terrace, or spa — before heading out for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Greek yogurt with thyme honey and walnuts, fresh fruit, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Packed picnic from a local deli or minimarket — olives, local cheese, bread, cherry tomatoes, and cold water (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Lively local psarotaverna (fish taverna) — fried calamari, shrimp saganaki, and grilled swordfish with a glass of local rosé (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm boat trip departure times the evening before. Bring a dry bag for valuables on the boat. Snorkeling gear can often be rented from the boat operator for €5–8.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local open-air market (laiki agora) in the nearest town. Browse stalls selling fresh produce, local cheeses, honey, herbs, and handmade goods. A great opportunity to interact with locals and pick up affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the town's old quarter on foot — whitewashed alleys, bougainvillea-draped walls, a small Byzantine church, and a central plateia (square). Stop at a traditional kafeneion (coffee house) for a Greek coffee and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class or food tasting experience focused on Greek mezedes and traditional recipes. Many local operators offer 2–3 hour evening sessions (€35–55 per person).

meals.breakfast: Local bakery near the market — tiropita (cheese pie), koulouri (sesame bread ring), and Greek coffee (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Taverna in the town square — moussaka, horiatiki salad, and a cold Alfa beer (€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Cooking class includes a shared meal of what you prepared — typically mezedes, dips, grilled meats, and local wine

day_by_day.notes: Markets typically run from 07:00–14:00 and are most vibrant before 10:00 AM. Bring a small tote bag for market purchases. Book the cooking class at least 2 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning at a different stretch of coastline — ask hotel staff for their favorite local beach recommendation. Arrive early to claim a good spot before crowds build up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter or ATV (€25–40/day) and explore the coastal road and inland villages at your own pace. Stop at viewpoints, small chapels, and olive groves along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Return the rental and head to a rooftop restaurant or elevated terrace restaurant for dinner with scenic views. Dress slightly smarter for a more relaxed-upscale experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — omelets, fresh juice, pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Village kafeneion or small taverna discovered on the scooter ride — whatever the daily special is (€10–15 per person)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant — lamb chops with rosemary, roasted vegetables, tzatziki, and a bottle of local Xinomavro red wine (€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: A valid driver's license is required for scooter/ATV rental. Helmets are mandatory. Fill up on fuel before heading into rural areas. Carry water and sunscreen for the ride.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning at the hotel pool or beach. This is the midpoint of the trip — a perfect day to recharge, journal, read, or simply float in the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local winery or olive oil producer for a guided tasting tour. Greece's indigenous grape varieties and single-estate olive oils are world-class and very affordable to taste locally (€10–20 per person for tasting sessions).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a highly-rated local restaurant recommended by hotel staff — focus on traditional Greek cuisine using seasonal, locally sourced ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed hotel breakfast — full spread with cold cuts, cheeses, eggs, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Winery or estate lunch pairing — local cheeses, charcuterie, bread, and wine (often included in tasting fee or €15–20 extra)
meals.dinner: Recommended local restaurant — slow-cooked lamb kleftiko, gigantes plaki (giant baked beans), and a shared dessert of galaktoboureko (custard pastry) with Greek coffee (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead to confirm winery or olive oil estate visiting hours and whether reservations are needed. Some estates require a minimum group size for tours.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided morning snorkeling or beginner scuba diving session at a local dive center. The warm, clear June waters offer excellent visibility for marine life and underwater rock formations (snorkeling: €20–30; intro dive: €50–70).
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on the beach post-dive. Afternoon is ideal for a light nap, beach read, and a refreshing swim. Visit a beach bar for a frappe or fresh watermelon juice.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the harbor or marina area and watch fishing boats return with the day's catch. Find a dockside taverna and ask what's freshest — order whatever the fisherman brought in that day.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-dive breakfast at the hotel — yogurt, banana, and water
meals.lunch: Beach bar — club sandwich, Greek salad, and a cold frappe coffee (€12–16 per person)
meals.dinner: Dockside fish taverna — catch of the day (priced by weight, typically €18–25), grilled with lemon and olive oil, plus a carafe of local white wine

day_by_day.notes: Avoid heavy meals before diving or snorkeling. Dive centers require a medical declaration — bring any relevant health information. Book dive sessions the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby larger town or city for cultural exploration. Visit the local archaeological museum (€4–8), a Venetian fortress or Byzantine church, and the historic center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the town — browse local shops for ceramic pottery, handwoven textiles, and local products like saffron, mountain herbs, and thyme honey. Have a long, leisurely lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a quiet evening on the hotel terrace or balcony with a bottle of local wine purchased during the day trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing for the day trip
meals.lunch: Town-center taverna — pastitsio (Greek lasagna), dakos (Cretan rusk salad), and a cold beer (€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Light and relaxed — hotel restaurant or room dining with local cheese, olives, bread, and wine from your shopping haul (€10–15 self-catered)

day_by_day.notes: Check local bus or taxi schedules in advance for the day trip. Many towns have reduced afternoon hours for shops (13:00–17:00 siesta time). Plan museum visits for the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach walk before breakfast — the early morning light on the Aegean is spectacular and the beach is nearly empty. Collect sea glass or shells as a free natural souvenir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try a stand-up paddleboard yoga session or beach volleyball if available through the hotel or local operators. Alternatively, find a shaded beach cove for a quieter, more private swim.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner experience — a restaurant with a tasting menu or a particularly scenic setting. This is a great evening to celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: Post-walk hotel breakfast — full spread with fresh-squeezed orange juice and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Beach taverna — grilled sardines, village bread, and a cold Mythos beer (€12–16 per person)
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual restaurant — multi-course Greek tasting menu featuring seasonal dishes, paired wines, and a dessert of loukoumades (honey donuts) (€40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Reserve the nicer dinner restaurant at least 2–3 days in advance, especially for a window or terrace table. Dress smart-casual for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — return to your favorite beach discovered during the trip. Swim, float, and soak in the atmosphere one last time before the trip winds down.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping and final exploration of local shops. Pick up olive oil, local honey, dried herbs, ceramic pieces, or evil eye charms as gifts. Visit a local deli to pack some Greek products for home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the first taverna you visited on Day 2 — a full-circle moment. Order everything you loved during the trip and toast to Greece.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — final leisurely morning meal with all the Greek favorites
meals.lunch: Light mezedes lunch at a café — hummus, taramosalata, grilled pita, and olives (€10–14 per person)
meals.dinner: Return to the Day 2 taverna — a celebratory spread of your trip favorites: grilled octopus, lamb chops, village salad, and a bottle of Assyrtiko to finish (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pack any fragile souvenirs like ceramics carefully with clothing padding. Check airline liquid restrictions for olive oil and honey quantities. Keep receipts for customs if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Final swim in the Aegean Sea — make it count. Pack up the room and check out of the hotel. Store luggage with the hotel concierge if checkout is before your departure time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend remaining local currency at a beachside café or wander the promenade one last time. Grab a final frappe or Greek coffee and sit by the sea in quiet reflection.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to the airport or ferry port for onward travel. Arrive with plenty of time for check-in and security. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Greek products.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — go back for seconds on the yogurt and honey
meals.lunch: Airport or port — spanakopita and a cold drink from a café (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or grab-and-go — light meal before the flight (€12–18)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange luggage storage if needed. Keep travel documents, boarding passes, and passports easily accessible. Allow extra time for airport security in summer peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — in transit home. Reflect on the incredible 13 days spent exploring Greece's beaches, flavors, and coastal culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: In transit or arrived home. Unpack your Greek treasures — olive oil, honey, herbs, and ceramics — and start planning your next visit.
day_by_day.evening: Settle back in at home. Recreate a simple Greek meal with your purchased ingredients — feta, olives, bread, and olive oil — to extend the Greek experience just a little longer.

meals.breakfast: Airport or in-flight meal
meals.lunch: In-flight or airport layover meal
meals.dinner: Home-cooked Greek-inspired meal using products brought back from Greece

day_by_day.notes: Greece will leave you wanting to return — start a wish list of islands and regions to explore on your next trip. Kalό taxídi — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, white sand, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boats depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets in Monastiraki. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek street food like souvlaki and spanakopita. Engage with local vendors and discover authentic Greek culinary culture.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade through the warm, calm waters of the lagoon and relax on one of Greece's most beautiful and unique beaches. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to escort you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink at the resort's bar.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — charcuterie board, olives, local cheeses, and a glass of Assyrtiko white wine to begin your Greek experience

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in amenities such as chilled towels, welcome fruit, and a bottle of local wine in the room. Keep the first night relaxed — no early morning commitments tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront to acclimate to the surroundings. Spend time at the resort's private beach — swim in the warm Aegean Sea and settle into the luxury of your beachfront accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area around the resort. Visit a nearby village for a relaxed stroll through whitewashed lanes, boutique shops, and local art galleries. Stop at a clifftop viewpoint for panoramic Aegean views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's infinity pool bar, followed by a welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Lavish breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — Greek yogurt with Cretan honey, fresh figs, spanakopita, smoked salmon, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Light poolside mezze lunch at the resort — tzatziki, grilled octopus, dolmades, and a chilled glass of Santorini Assyrtiko
meals.dinner: Signature restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort — slow-roasted lamb with herbs, fresh catch of the day, and a curated Greek wine pairing menu

day_by_day.notes: This is your recovery and orientation day. Avoid over-scheduling. Confirm upcoming excursion bookings with the resort concierge — especially boat tours and food experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour: Depart early by private transfer to Athens. Begin an immersive guided food tour of the Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) in Monastiraki. Explore stalls overflowing with fresh fish, spices, olives, and local produce. Meet vendors, taste cured meats, artisan cheeses, and freshly baked koulouri bread.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the food tour through the surrounding streets of Monastiraki and Psiri neighborhoods. Sample souvlaki, loukoumades (Greek honey doughnuts), and regional wines at curated stops. Explore the Monastiraki Flea Market for unique artisan souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Athens' top fine-dining restaurants in the Kolonaki or Syntagma district, with views of the illuminated Acropolis. Return to the resort by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort before departure — Greek pastries, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Athens Central Market Food Tour — a progressive tasting journey through authentic market stalls and local eateries in Monastiraki
meals.dinner: Dinner at Varoulko Seaside or Spondi (Athens) — modern Greek fine dining with a Michelin-star pedigree; expect dishes like sea urchin pasta, slow-cooked suckling pig, and an extensive Greek wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the Athens food tour with a premium private guide for an exclusive experience. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Carry a small bag for market purchases. Private round-trip transfer from resort to Athens recommended — approximately 30–60 minutes depending on resort location.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat charter departure for a full-day island-hopping cruise around the local Aegean islands. Begin with a morning sail through crystal-clear turquoise waters, anchoring at a secluded cove for an exclusive swim and snorkel session away from crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the private charter to a nearby island or coastal village. Disembark for a guided walk through a traditional fishing village, visit a local taverna on the waterfront, and explore a hillside monastery or ancient ruins accessible only by sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by boat at sunset. Enjoy a private beachfront dinner arranged by the resort — candlelit table on the sand, fresh seafood grilled to order, and a bottle of premium Greek wine.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Onboard the private charter — a catered gourmet Greek picnic with grilled fish, fresh salads, local bread, olives, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — whole grilled sea bass, lobster with lemon butter, Greek salad with barrel-aged feta, and a bottle of Domaine Sigalas Santorini Assyrtiko

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter at least 1–2 weeks in advance through the resort concierge. Apply high-SPF sunscreen throughout the day. Bring a hat, sunglasses, and a light cover-up. Snorkeling equipment can typically be provided by the charter.

day_by_day.morning: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit: Depart by private speedboat or luxury charter to Zakynthos for the iconic Navagio Beach experience. Arrive early to beat the crowds and witness the dramatic limestone cliffs and the famous shipwreck on the pristine white sand in golden morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim in the extraordinarily clear turquoise waters of Navagio Beach. Explore the sea caves and blue grottos along the Zakynthos coastline by boat. Stop at a secluded beach accessible only by sea for a private afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return from Zakynthos. Freshen up at the resort and enjoy a relaxed evening at the resort's rooftop or terrace bar with Aegean sunset views and signature cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at resort before departure — Greek yogurt, honey, fresh fruit, and espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium waterfront restaurant in Zakynthos town or Porto Vromi — grilled calamari, fresh fish of the day, village salad, and local white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's terrace restaurant — lamb chops with rosemary and lemon, roasted vegetables, and a dessert of baklava with vanilla ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach is only accessible by boat — no road access. Arrange the boat tour through the resort concierge or a premium charter company. The beach can get very busy midday; arriving early is strongly recommended. Bring waterproof bags for electronics.

day_by_day.morning: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip: Depart by private transfer to the southwestern coast of Crete to visit the legendary Elafonissi Beach. Arrive early to enjoy the famous pink-tinged sand and shallow, warm lagoon waters in relative tranquility. Wade across the shallow sandbar to the small island of Elafonissi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on the beach — swim in the warm, shallow turquoise lagoon, snorkel around the rocky outcrops, and explore the wild dunes and natural landscape of the Elafonissi nature reserve.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by private transfer. Enjoy a spa treatment at the resort's luxury wellness center — a traditional Greek massage or Aegean salt scrub — followed by a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort before departure
meals.lunch: Premium beachside lunch near Elafonissi — fresh seafood mezze, grilled fish, horiatiki salad, and chilled Cretan rosé at a quality taverna near the beach
meals.dinner: Intimate dinner at a local fine-dining restaurant near the resort — Cretan cuisine featuring dakos (barley rusk salad), braised goat with stamnagathi greens, and local Vidiano white wine

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is approximately 1.5–2 hours from Heraklion by car. A private driver is strongly recommended. Arrive before 10:00 AM to secure a premium spot. The pink sand effect is most visible in calm, shallow water near the shore. Book spa treatments in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated resort relaxation morning — sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and spend time at the private beach. Optional: sunrise yoga or meditation session on the beach (available through resort wellness program).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Greek cooking class arranged through the resort or a local culinary school. Learn to prepare traditional dishes such as moussaka, spanakopita, fresh tzatziki, and loukoumades with a professional Greek chef using local market ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the meal you prepared during the cooking class in a private dining setting — either at the cooking school or arranged back at the resort. Pair with selected Greek wines.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast at the resort — full spread including eggs to order, smoked fish, pastries, fresh juices, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch at the resort pool bar — hummus, pita, grilled vegetables, and a refreshing Aperol Spritz
meals.dinner: The dishes from your afternoon cooking class — moussaka, spanakopita, fresh salads — enjoyed in a private setting with a curated Greek wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Book the private cooking class at least 3–4 days in advance. Classes typically last 3–4 hours including eating. This is a wonderful mid-trip day to slow down, reconnect with the destination's culinary culture, and recharge for the second week.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of a nearby ancient archaeological site — a hilltop acropolis, Minoan palace ruins, or Byzantine monastery depending on the resort's location. Travel by private vehicle with a licensed archaeologist or historian guide for an exclusive, in-depth experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive oil estate or winery for a premium tasting experience. Tour the vineyard or olive groves, learn about traditional Greek production methods, and enjoy a guided tasting of award-winning Greek wines or extra-virgin olive oils paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Sunset drinks on the resort terrace followed by dinner at a highly-rated local restaurant in the nearest town or village.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Included tasting lunch at the winery or olive estate — artisan cheeses, cured meats, fresh bread, olives, and wine or olive oil tastings
meals.dinner: Dinner at a top-rated local restaurant — stuffed peppers with rice and herbs, fresh grilled fish, and a dessert of galaktoboureko (custard pastry) with local thyme honey

day_by_day.notes: Request an exclusive private tour at the archaeological site to avoid tour groups. Many premium Greek wineries — such as those in Nemea, Santorini, or Crete — offer private tastings with advance reservation. Ask the resort concierge for the best local options.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning stand-up paddleboarding or kayaking excursion along the coastline, departing from the resort's private beach. Explore hidden coves, sea caves, and rocky outcrops inaccessible by foot. Guided by a water sports instructor from the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local artisan market or ceramics workshop in a nearby village. Watch craftspeople at work and purchase handmade Greek pottery, jewelry, or textiles as premium souvenirs. Stroll through the village and stop at a traditional kafeneion (coffee house) for a Greek coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset sailing experience — a 2-hour luxury catamaran or sailboat cruise along the coastline at golden hour, with champagne and canapés on deck.

meals.breakfast: Light early breakfast at resort before water sports — yogurt, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a family-run taverna in the village — fresh pasta with seafood, grilled sardines, village bread, and a carafe of local white wine
meals.dinner: Return to resort for dinner at the signature restaurant — a tasting menu featuring seasonal Greek ingredients, paired with a sommelier-curated Greek wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset sailing cruise through the resort concierge — private charters are significantly more exclusive than group tours. Water sports equipment is typically available through the resort's beach club. Bring a light jacket for the evening boat cruise.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to a premium destination island or coastal town by private speedboat or ferry. Explore the island's main town — wander through Venetian or Cycladic architecture, visit a hilltop fortress or windmills, and browse luxury boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Discover the island's most beautiful beach by private boat — anchor offshore and swim in secluded waters. Alternatively, hire a local guide for a hike to a dramatic viewpoint with panoramic island and sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the island's most celebrated restaurant before returning to the resort by private transfer or boat.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort before departure
meals.lunch: Waterfront lunch at a premium taverna on the island — fresh lobster, grilled octopus, fava bean dip, and chilled local wine
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the island's top restaurant — contemporary Greek cuisine with locally sourced ingredients, exceptional sea views, and an extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: Island selection depends on the resort's location — Mykonos, Santorini, Paros, Corfu, or Rhodes are all excellent options. Confirm travel logistics (boat or ferry schedules) with the concierge at least 2 days in advance. Carry a small daypack with essentials.

day_by_day.morning: Resort spa morning — indulge in a full luxury wellness experience. Choose from a deep-tissue massage, traditional hammam ritual, thalassotherapy (seawater therapy), or a signature Aegean treatment using local herbs, sea salt, and olive oil.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided food and wine tour of the local area — visit a local market, a traditional cheese producer, a honey farm, or a seafood market. End with a curated tasting session pairing regional foods with premium Greek wines.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private chef dinner on the resort's private beach or terrace — a bespoke menu designed around your food preferences, prepared tableside with theatrical flair.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — leisurely and indulgent, with all your favorites
meals.lunch: Included in the afternoon food and wine tour — progressive tastings of local honey, cheese, charcuterie, and wine
meals.dinner: Private chef beach dinner — freshly caught whole fish, premium Greek meats, seasonal vegetables, artisan bread, and a hand-selected bottle of aged Greek wine under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Book the private chef beach dinner experience at least 3–4 days in advance through the resort. This is one of the most memorable experiences of the trip — consider pairing it with a special occasion celebration if applicable. Spa bookings should also be made several days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day at the resort's private beach. Spend the morning swimming, sunbathing, and savoring the Aegean in complete luxury. Rent a private cabana with dedicated beach butler service for the ultimate experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping and exploration of the local area — pick up premium Greek products to take home: extra-virgin olive oil, aged feta, local wines, Mastiha liqueur, and artisan honey. Visit a local jewelry boutique for handmade gold Greek-inspired pieces.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort's finest dining venue or a celebrated local restaurant — a celebratory meal to close out an extraordinary trip.

meals.breakfast: Extended final breakfast at the resort — order everything you loved throughout the trip
meals.lunch: Poolside or beachside lunch at the resort — grilled calamari, Greek salad, fresh pita, and a final glass of Assyrtiko
meals.dinner: Farewell fine-dining dinner — a multi-course tasting menu with wine pairing, celebrating 12 days of Greece's finest beaches, food, and culture

day_by_day.notes: Pack non-essentials the night before departure to make the final morning stress-free. Confirm airport transfer timing with the concierge. Purchase any last-minute gifts or premium Greek food products today. Arrange for luggage to be collected from the room early if departing the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at the resort — enjoy one last swim in the Aegean Sea and a relaxed breakfast. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and depart by private luxury transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure — travel day. Arrive at the airport with ample time for a smooth, stress-free departure. Relax in the premium airport lounge before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry your memories of 13 extraordinary days in Greece — the turquoise waters of Navagio, the pink sands of Elafonissi, the flavors of Athens' markets, and the warmth of the Aegean sun.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at the resort — Greek yogurt, local honey, fresh pastries, fruit, and a perfect Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Premium airport lounge or a final café stop near the airport — light snacks, mezze, and refreshments
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout from the resort if your flight departs in the afternoon or evening — most luxury resorts accommodate this with advance notice. Confirm private airport transfer the night before. Keep one carry-on bag accessible for any premium Greek food items purchased. Allow extra time at airport security for any liquids (olive oil, wine) in checked luggage.
